html:
SMTO-LLM-0092 — SMTO couldn't confirm your model service's security certificate

GUID: 9fd8f0ef-f41c-40ea-8dd9-5c3c46efab04
Slug: llm-tls-verification-failed
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: readiness

What happened

  • SMTO stopped the connection because it couldn't confirm that the secure connection really belongs to your model service. No answer came back from the model.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and check that the failing model's Endpoint uses the exact server name the model service was set up with, not a different name or a number address such as 192.168.1.20. A certificate is valid only for specific server names, so a mismatched address fails this check.
  2. Ask the person who runs the model service to check that its certificate hasn't expired and that the full certificate chain is installed. An expired or incomplete certificate is the most common reason this check fails.
  3. If your organization issues its own certificates, ask the person who manages SMTO to add that issuer to the trusted certificates on the computer running SMTO. SMTO only trusts certificates it can trace back to an issuer that computer already trusts.
  4. Select Check saved model on that model's card. It confirms SMTO can now verify the certificate and get an answer.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model completes without a certificate error, and new tasks get answers from the model.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the model service. Don't turn off certificate checking to get past this; it protects your data from being read or changed on the way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • TLS certificate verification failed while connecting to the model service (for example an untrusted or missing issuer, an expired certificate, or a hostname mismatch).

What this means

  • The certificate could not be validated for the requested host with the current trust store. A missing issuer, expired certificate or hostname mismatch can cause this failure. It does not establish a model or token-budget problem.

Why this can happen

  • The certificate could not be validated for the requested host with the current trust store. A missing issuer, expired certificate or hostname mismatch can cause this failure. It does not establish a model or token-budget problem.

How to diagnose it

  • TLS certificate verification failed while connecting to the model service.
  • A model request from the SMTO process verifies the certificate and completes.

How to fix it

  • Check that the role's base URL hostname matches the certificate's names and that the certificate is within its validity dates. Have the service install the full certificate chain, or add the private CA to the trust store used by the SMTO Server process (the system store or SSL_CERT_FILE). Keep certificate verification enabled.
  • Verify the HTTPS hostname and certificate dates. Ask the service administrator to install the complete certificate chain or configure the trusted private CA for the SMTO process. Keep certificate verification enabled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition before trying the affected request again. Inspect existing operation receipts before resuming saved work.

How to verify the fix

  • A model request from the SMTO process verifies the certificate and completes.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
